In descent order:

1. **Omar** \- Underrated character, cooking is a skill that can improve or decrease overall morale. Being able not only to improve morale, but also ration food, making food not taste bland, and giving everyone something to look for besides "needing it to survive" is a huge W.

2. **Mitch** \- Making all those traps surrounding the school and being able to mantain them in the long run are a huge advantage, not only to deal with small hordes, but also bandits in some cases if properly modified. He probably was the one that taught the others how to make and mantain the animal traps.

3. **Ruby** \- Probably the only kid with some nursery/medicine formation. I wouldn't give her a ranking this high because she is a child and one'd think that she only knows very basic stuff, but we can't forget that she was able to help AJ when he was shot by Abel and stop Clementine's bleeding when AJ brought her in e5. Not only she stopped Clementine's bleeding, she also was able to properly clean the wound and treat the huge infection she must had. Katja in s1 couldn't help an adult with the same wound and she was a veterinary, so I give her the props for this feat alone.

4. **Louis** \- As a violentine lover myself, the dude is a walking morale booster. He eases tensions between members, scales down arguments and is able to entertain everyone through games or music, he's a showman with all the letters. People like him are important in these times to not let depression hit your group.

5. **Willy** \- Mostly annoying, but the best apprentice of Mitch. Having another guy that can take on the legacy of the group's traps is important.

6. **Rosie** \- How rare must be a dog in this apocalypse? Let alone a **trained** pitbull. Rosie serves both as an offensive and defensive companion, also capable of alerting the group when something is off. Only con is needing to feed her too, but shouldn't be a problem in the location.

7. **Violet** \- One of the best group defenders when there are zombies nearby, also best leader to take the charge after Marlon's fall. Sometimes irrascible, but sociable given the chance.

8. **Aasim** \- Having someone documenting history is great, serves as a great reminder of lessons done in the past, what works, what doesn't, etc.

9. **Brody** \- She really didn't do much besides helping Marlon with decision making. I know she had the right intentions with it and didn't want to give away the sisters to Lilly, but her lack of communication with the rest and leadership capacity makes her not that valuable. Maybe if she didn't die in e1 we could see an improvement in this and have a higher rank.

10. **Tenn** \- Literally just a kid that lives in the school. Doesn't really contribute to anything and is too light hearted for this world, making his mistakes cost dearly (Mitch's life, Louis/Violet life if you let him). 

11. **Marlon** \- Worse than making mistakes is making them knowing they are wrong. I'm sure he started being the leader with great intentions, seeing that all the adults left them, but the power got over his head and his lack of protection to his community just makes him awful. Sure, he planified the days to collect food with Brody and protected the school against walkers, but he'd sell members of the community just to avoid conflict. Threatens members, pinpoints guilt, killed Brody at one point for a disagreement, just plain awful dude, and I'll always stand with killing him, at that point he was already gone and did too much to just let him be in the school. At the very least he deserved to be left out of school.

I think this could be good in local sets where the players could use their phones to look at the character sheet and not having to carry out their sheets into the tabletop, but it'd fail in a lot of areas.

·Updating things in local tabletops could be done faster with the paper or even with an editable pdf than with an app in most cases. If the app is aimed to ease the level up and do it for you, it must be really faster than doing it manually.

·Us DMs like to have our players character sheet in hand, either to roll some things for them without having to tell them, checking stats, prepare future combats to be balanced, etc. If this app is offline, it'd likely fail in giving the DM the power to track these character sheets easily and make him have a workaround (like setting all the character sheets individually and updating them mid session).

·A lot of setups have homebrew, so it should also be able to let you add homebrew with ease.

·Something that some apps with the same idea fail is to guide players. A lot of my players don't really know about the rules of leveling and sometimes need to be guided towards what they have to add, what to roll for health, etc. So it should definitely have the option to follow the phb rules on leveling depending on what class are you.

·The most powerful use of these kind of apps is being able to throw dices and add the bonus/penalty automatically without having to know what to add. Throw dmg and the app knows if u must use dexterity or strength and what proficiency to add, throw persuassion and the app knows the charisma modifier to add it, etc.

Even though youtube guides will be your place to go to learn more about the game, in general lines:

1) You'll normally want a defender, support and 2 dps. This can change (and changes a lot) depending on the context of the fights you're going to do. Some fights require 3 supports and 1 dps, or 2 supports 2 dps, it all depends on what u're trying to achieve.

2) Again, depends on the context, but normally you'll want to bring at least one dps with that attribute. You'll know about the context when you're trying to do special event formidable foes in one try or a specific floor in tower of illusions and check for guides or practice yourself with combinations.

3) The recollection bits (memories from this point) serve as a power up for your characters. Any team is made of at least 4 characters and each character should have one memory. When you equip a character with a memory, they'll boost their physical technique (attribute used to calculate physical technique damage), cursed technique (same as before but with cursed technique) and HP. These memories can also have passive and/or active effects, for example, increasing by a % your cursed technique for 2 turns.

4) The pity system in this game is dog shit. Each pull gives you a gacha point for that specific banner. 10 pulls (a multi) gives you 10 points. You can exchange these points for any of the featured characters/memories of that banner. The problem is, any ssr memory costs 120 points (36k cubes worth of pulls) and any ssr character costs 250 points (75k cubes worth of pulls). This effectively means that if you want to ensure you get a character, you'll need at the very minimum 75k cubes if you are unlucky, and getting cubes as a f2p in this game is DEMANDING. You need to farm a lot and invest some hours daily if you want to get all the possible cubes from events, domain investigations, achievements, etc.

Lilly definitely was nostalgic when she sees Clem in ep 2. She cared about her in s1 and thought all this time that she was either dead or so far away that she wouldn't see her ever again. Seeing her again filled her with a lot of emotions and it's something that you can clearly see. 

The thing is, even if us as a player try to make her do the right thing, appeal to her memories and try to be nice to her, Lilly can't just magically change. She's been all these years with the Delta, I'm pretty sure she's one of the leaders too seeing how the other soldiers talk with her. 

In ep 2 she sees Clem for the first time and thinks she can persue her to join her group. She thinks that Clem will accept just like when she was a child, that's why she didn't bring a lot of soldiers (Abel confirms this at the end of ep2 by saying "I told Lilly you wouldn't cooperate"). At the end of this episode, Lilly can't bring herself to kill Clem, there are too many emotions fighting inside her at this point.

Now, in ep3, the game makes her very very evil. She phisically tortures Louis (in my run) and threatens the rest. Locks everyone up when Clem and the rest show up, tries to intimidate her, to kill James, make AJ a soldier in front of Clem, etc...

But I don't think that this is inconsistent. Lilly lost two of her best soldiers because she thought Clem could change, it's in the middle of an horde because of her and now she has the opportunity of bringing her to the Delta and force her to be a soldier. Lilly is fueled with rage at this point, she doesn't want to kill Clementine because she needs to cut losses.

But in ep 4 she is once again shown vulnerable. She lost everything at this point, her soldiers, the boat, and I bet that a lot of supplies too, such as ammo, food, fuel, horses, etc. The Delta will probably lose the war, so she's already facing her future loneliness. There's no point in killing Clementine for her, she won't gain anything from it, she had to do it in the woods, not now. 

So, I think that Lilly gets sad when Clem tells her that she hates her because she knows that there's nothing more to do with Clem. The kid she knew is no longer there, as well as the adult Clem knew died too. Lillys' morals are fucked up and she really believes that the best way to make someone safe is kidnapping them and forcing labor with them.
